correctness.rationale: For \(A,B\in T_3(\mathbb F_q)\), the commutator coordinates reduce to two determinant equations and one affine linear equation. The determinant fiber counts are \(D(0)=q(q^2+q-1)\) and \(D(c)=q(q^2-1)\) for \(c\ne0\). On the exceptional locus where the last linear coefficients vanish, a basis calculation with three vectors in \(\mathbb F_q^2\) gives \(K=q^4-q^2\) off the central axis, \(K=2q^4-q^2\) on it, \(H=q(q^2-1)\) for every nonzero target, and \(H=q^4+q^3-q\) at zero. Substitution gives the four stated fibers. Their target-weighted sum is \(q^{12}\). The packaged verifier independently exhausts \(q=2,3,5\) effective coordinates and all \(q=2\) matrix pairs.

value.rationale: The fixed-target distribution is a natural refinement of the classical commuting probability. \(T_3\) is the first full triangular algebra whose radical has nonzero square, so the bilinear term \(pu-sr\) changes the commutator fibers in a structural way. The four-stratum theorem explains that change uniformly over every finite field and yields a complete word-map distribution, not a small or arbitrary parameter slice.
